advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make TransientRetryBudget's exhausted branch defensive about an empty transient_cell (assert or raise a clear error) so an empty cell cannot silently downgrade a pass-abort to a 'failed' tally.
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/retry_budget.py:162: if plan.action == "exhausted" and self._transient_cell[0] is not None:
advisory.finding: TransientRetryBudget.attempt_retry only re-raises when `plan.action == 'exhausted' and self._transient_cell[0] is not None`; when the cell is None at exhaustion it silently returns the exhausted plan, which the coordinator maps to Disposition.exhausted_transient (the 'failed' bucket) instead of aborting the pass. This only stays correct under the sequential single-op invariant (the last failed dispatch always leaves its exc in the cell). The silent fall-through is not asserted against, so a future wiring change that cleared or shared the cell differently would convert a pass-abort into a quiet 'failed' tally.
advisory.suggested_fix: On `plan.action == 'exhausted'`, assert `self._transient_cell[0] is not None` (or raise a RuntimeError naming the invariant) before re-raising, so an unexpected empty cell fails loudly instead of returning the exhausted plan.
